AnswerAll.confirmText: Every pair on this page with no answer gets it, as if its own button were pressed; a pair the answer on another one already decided is left as it is. Each answer goes into the journal and can be taken back in its row.
AnswerAll.hint: Answer “{{word}}” on every pair left on this page, after a confirmation
AnswerAll.label_one: The {{count}} pair left on this page, all at once:
AnswerAll.label_other: The {{count}} pairs left on this page, all at once:
DuplicatesScreen.description: Of every work, its likeliest pair of one work and its likeliest pair of one series among the works of every site, its own too: every field the sites share is compared, the text itself aside — the title, the description, the tags, universes, characters, pairings, the status and other values, the size. First the pairs where the score by the formula of the work the pair was looked for times the chance the pair is one work is higher. "One work" links them as the work's window does: the grade and the interest become shared. "Different" — the pair is offered no more. The answers teach the models of the chances.
DuplicatesScreen.journalHint: Every answer on a pair and every answer taken back, the newest first, to undo
DuplicatesScreen.learntHint: The chance of one work is a model fitted on your answers "one work" and "different"; fitted again a few seconds after an answer
DuplicatesScreen.neverSearched: The pairs were never looked for yet. Press "Search again".
DuplicatesScreen.noneChosen: No pairs of the answers chosen
DuplicatesScreen.notLearntHint: No pair is marked "one work" yet: in place of the chance, the mean likeness of the shared layers
DuplicatesScreen.searchHint: Compare every work of every site anew, by the vectors of their titles and descriptions as they are now. In the background, in the queue of the computations; the answers are kept
DuplicatesScreen.shownHint: Which pairs are shown by their answer: unanswered, and of each answer. «Different» alone sorted by «one series», say, to look through those said different again, the likeliest of one series first. The choice is kept in the browser
DuplicatesScreen.sortHint: What the chance of one work is multiplied by: the interest and the predicted grade of the work the pair was looked for (of both, when each is the other's likeliest, the larger). The choice is kept in the browser
DuplicatesScreen.title: Duplicates across the sites
PairGrid.allowedHint: The site names the values the work may have — it has one of them: the works agree when such values meet (green: "=" the same, "⊂" one within the other, "∩" some in common), and differ when none are in common (red "≠")
PairGrid.facetHint: How alike the values are {{value}}; a rare value weighs more than a common one. All in common green, none red, some yellow
PairGrid.noAuthorHint: The authors of one of the works are not known: nothing to compare
PairGrid.notComparedHint: Not of both works: nothing to compare
PairGrid.notMeasuredHint: The texts are not encoded yet: how alike they mean is not measured yet
PairGrid.otherAuthorHint: Both works have their authors, and the dictionary of authors gives them none in common: most likely different authors
PairGrid.sameAuthorHint: The dictionary of authors gives the works an author in common: one normalized author, or authors marked as partly one
PairGrid.sameTextHint: The texts are not encoded yet: they are the same word for word
PairGrid.siteFandomsHint: The fandom as the site names it: the application knows no universe of the work
PairGrid.sizeHint: The sizes differ by {{value}} (the smaller over the larger by words, characters and parts, on average): up to 5 % green, up to 10 % yellow, more red
PairGrid.textHint: How alike the two texts mean {{value}} (the cosine of their vectors): from 95 % green, from 85 % yellow, below red. Of the pairs said different, the middle ones have about 76 % of titles and 58 % of descriptions
PairGrid.title: Title
PairGrid.valuesHint: {{value}} values in common: all green, none red, some yellow
PairJournal.description: Every answer on a pair — here or in a work's window — and every answer taken back, the newest first. The last answer on a pair can be undone while it stands: the pair gets back what it had before.
PairJournal.failed: The journal could not be read: {{error}}
PairJournal.restoredHint: Answered before the journal existed and restored from what was kept: the time is the kept one, the pair one page of each work, what the pair had before is unknown. Undoing takes the answer back
PairJournal.undoHint: Give the pair back what it had before this answer: {{word}}
PairRow.chanceHint: The chance this is one work: by the model of your answers (before the first "one work", the mean likeness of the layers)
PairRow.derivedHint: No word of its own: both works are of one series — a site's series, or other pairs said «One series». It weighs as one said. «Different» or taking the word back takes out of the series only the works you put in it: a site's series keeps its works
PairRow.differentHint: These are different works: a link, if any, is taken away, the pair is offered no more
PairRow.partialHint: One holds a part of the other's text — a site has not all its chapters, say, or one is a collection the other is in (the volumes of a series are «One series»): each its own grade and interest; the pair is not offered again, the model does not learn from it
PairRow.priorityHint: The score by the formula of the work the pair was looked for (of both, when each is the other's likeliest, the larger) times the chance of one work: what the pairs are ordered by
PairRow.prioritySizeHint: The chance of one work times the mean size of the pair's two works in words (stated by their sites or worked out of their characters): the pairs are ordered by it
PairRow.relatedHint: Another relation of two works: a translation, a part, or one series
PairRow.sameHint: This is one work: link them as the work's window does; the grade and the interest become shared
PairRow.seriesChanceHint: The chance these are different works of one series, by the model of your answers «One series» (shown after the first such answer)
PairRow.seriesHint: These are different works of one series — volumes of one cycle, say: each its own grade and interest; the pair is not offered again. The model of a series learns from such answers; to the model of one work they are different works
PairRow.translationHint: One is the translation of the other: different works of one text, each its own grade and interest; the pair is offered no more. The model does not learn from translations: their authors differ, their tags and descriptions are one
PairRow.unanswerHint: Take the answer back: the link, "different", "translation" or "partly" goes, the pair returns to the unanswered
WorkSide.estimate: Worked out of the site's other number by how many words the work has to a character
